questions.scenario: A sewing operator and an accounts officer both earn ৳15,000/month. Why does only the operator's wage enter garment cost?
options: Because operators are paid weekly
Because her hours are TRACEABLE to specific orders (direct labor → WIP), while his work serves the whole company (admin → period expense)
Salaries under ৳20,000 never become product cost
It's a policy choice — either could be classified either way for convenience
questions.explanation: Attribution is the test: operator hours map to PO-2291's bucket; accounts work benefits no single garment. Same money, different routing, both honest.
wrongExplanations: Pay frequency has nothing to do with cost behavior.
Amount thresholds aren't classification logic — traceability is.
Classification follows economic truth; convenience-classification is how pricing lies begin.

questions.scenario: A dyeing floor supervisor cannot be attributed to any single order. His salary becomes:
options: Direct labor on the largest order
Factory overhead — pooled and applied to products via drivers like machine hours
Marketing expense
Nobody's cost at all
questions.explanation: Essential-but-shared production support = indirect factory labor = OH pool (Module 5). Products still carry him — just spread fairly instead of traced exactly.
wrongExplanations: 'Biggest order' attribution is arbitrary fiction.
He supervises PRODUCTION; selling costs are a different world.
His salary is very much someone's cost — shared by all units through application rates.

questions.scenario: Rule R8 posts August payroll. Which line combination is CORRECT for gross salaries of ৳94L, TDS withheld ৳3.6L, net paid later ৳90.4L?
options: Dr Salaries Expense 90.4L / Cr Bank 90.4L
Dr WIP-Direct Labor + Dr Factory OH + Dr Admin Salaries = 94L total / Cr TDS Payable 3.6L + Cr Salaries Payable 90.4L
Dr Cash 94L / Cr Salaries 94L
All 94L straight into WIP
questions.explanation: The fork in one entry: route each salary block to its destiny (WIP/OH/Admin), recognize the NBR liability for tax withheld, and the payable for net wages. Accrual first, payment later.
wrongExplanations: That expenses EVERYTHING immediately and ignores both the fork and the tax liability.
Backwards direction — cash hasn't moved yet on payroll day.
Admin salaries inside garments would make every tee pay for desks.

questions.scenario: Salaries for August are paid on September 5th. The EXPENSE belongs to:
options: September — pay day decides everything
August — when the work was EARNED (accrual accounting)
Split by whichever month has lower profit
December, with the annual bonus
questions.explanation: Matching again: costs belong to the period they helped. Payday timing only creates then clears a payable — the P&L never waits for the bank calendar.
wrongExplanations: Cash timing is Module 11's cash-flow story, not expense recognition.
Profit-shaping by convenience is misrepresentation.
Bonuses accrue monthly as provisions precisely so December isn't ambushed.

questions.scenario: Sewing line 4 reports heavy OT but output FELL 10%. Finance should treat this as:
options: Normal — overtime always means more output
An exception demanding reconciliation across production logs, attendance/OT authorizations, and downtime records before accepting the cost
Proof workers are thieves
A reason to delete the OT records
questions.explanation: Module 0's promise fulfilled: labor data must reconcile with physical output. Explanations exist (breakdowns, rework, complexity) — but they must be DOCUMENTED, not assumed.
wrongExplanations: OT without output is cost without product — the exact inconsistency audits sample for.
Accusations aren't analysis; multiple innocent causes compete with fraud.
Destroying records converts a puzzle into proven fraud.

questions.scenario: Assume an annual bonus obligation of ৳9,36,000 is earned evenly over twelve months. What does each monthly accrual do?
options: Pays the bonus early
Debit the appropriate production/admin cost and credit Bonus Payable ৳78,000; cash is paid separately later
Nothing — bonuses are expensed only when gifted
Transfers money to workers' wallets monthly
questions.explanation: ৳9,36,000 ÷ 12 = ৳78,000 per month. This exercise supplies the obligation and earning pattern; it does not assert a statutory percentage of gross payroll.
wrongExplanations: Provisioning reserves COST, not cash — payment still happens on schedule.
Expensing only at payout violates accrual and makes festival months lie.
Provisions are accounting entries, not cash transfers.

questions.scenario: WPPF (Workers' Profit Participation Fund) is best described as:
options: Optional charity from owners
A legally required share of company profit provisioned annually and credited to a fund for workers — accrued as an expense/liability of the business
A bank loan for employees
Part of export revenue
questions.explanation: Bangladesh law entitles workers to a slice of profit (5% pattern under WPPF rules). Accounting provisions it like bonus accruals — worker-wise registers track entitlements (Mizan) while GL carries the liability (Shirin).
wrongExplanations: It's statutory, not discretionary generosity.
No lending involved — it's earned profit-sharing.
It reduces distributable profit; it isn't income.

questions.scenario: An employee transfers from sewing to FG store mid-month; HR forgets to update his department code. Consequence:
options: None — payroll is one lump number anyway
His wages keep flowing into DIRECT labor/garment cost though he now works stores — overstating product cost and understating warehouse OH until corrected
The ERP auto-detects transfers physically
Salary stops entirely
questions.explanation: The employee master's department field IS the posting route. Stale codes silently reroute money between product cost and overhead pools — the fireside chat's warning made real.
wrongExplanations: Lump-sum payroll is precisely what costing cannot use.
Systems don't watch doors; masters drive postings.
He keeps earning — just possibly in the wrong GL direction.

questions.scenario: Which payroll design makes Masco's numbers trustworthy end-to-end?
options: One big salary total posted monthly
Biometric-backed attendance + OT pre-authorization tied to output logs + department-coded employee masters feeding categorized payroll files that R8 posts line-by-line
Trust-based self-reported hours
Annual estimation without monthly detail
questions.explanation: Every control links documents to money: biometrics prove presence, authorizations prove approval, output proves plausibility, masters route cost. That chain IS auditable payroll.
wrongExplanations: Lump sums hide direct/indirect splits — costing dies there.
Self-reporting invites the impossible-overtime scenario forever.
Estimates can't survive a single audit question.

questions.scenario: TDS on salaries (৳3.6L withheld) appears in the payroll entry as a CREDIT to 'TDS/Salary Tax Payable'. What does that credit represent?
options: Extra profit for Masco
Money deducted FROM employees that Masco now OWES to NBR on their behalf — cleared when the challan is paid
The workers' savings account
A discount from government
questions.explanation: Withholding creates a liability to the tax authority, not income. It sits in payable until deposited with the NBR challan — another document-driven lifecycle, same as supplier payments.
wrongExplanations: It's other people's tax passing through — never Masco's income.
It's owed to NBR, not saved for workers (their benefit statements show it as tax paid).
Governments collect; they don't discount payroll.
